summary: Configured persistent UFW on node1. SSH is allowed from any address; TCP/9000 is allowed only from node2 (10.100.18.11) and explicitly rejected for all other sources. Live tests confirmed node2 succeeds and node3 is rejected. All three nodes were restarted sequentially, showed changed boot IDs, and recovered healthy. Temporary test listeners were removed.
actions_performed: Enabled UFW persistently with default deny incoming and allow outgoing.
Allowed TCP/22 from any IPv4 or IPv6 address.
Allowed TCP/9000 from node2 before the catch-all rejection rule.
Rejected TCP/9000 from every other IPv4 or IPv6 source.
Verified filtering using a temporary listener on node1.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 individually and verified recovery.

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall and SSH allowed from any address
evidence.summary: UFW is active and enabled after reboot; TCP/22 has an Anywhere allow rule, and an SSH TCP connection succeeded.

evidence.requirement: TCP/9000 allowed only from node2 and rejected elsewhere
evidence.summary: After node1 reboot, node2 connected successfully while node3 received an immediate rejection. Live counters recorded two allows from node2 and two catch-all rejects.
Boot ID changed from 01c87a03-dbeb-4f85-a94d-30e88b180160 to 00ea6cf0-7c1f-425e-b169-dcc55ab84d5a; UFW and the complete policy recovered.
Boot ID changed from e8afb731-420c-4162-a989-583aca271335 to 1d38c376-3e58-40fe-a6bc-6a0cc9fa8805; networking recovered and node2 retained access to TCP/9000.
Boot ID changed from dfeb3b70-bc1e-4ce9-90d0-9c9c853416e7 to f59fbefb-c24c-49ee-9bd7-5f9924a7e9ec; networking recovered and TCP/9000 remained rejected.
